outcomes.original: Filing step: If Planning confirms the expansion requires a Conditional Use Authorization, file a CUA application with the Planning Department including a project description, floor plan, neighborhood outreach summary and environmental evaluation application. What to say: Frame the restaurant as a neighborhood-serving use that continues a 40-year food-service presence at the site, emphasize limited cooking with no late-night hours, commit to a community liaison during construction, and describe the expansion as filling underutilized retail space in a low-density restaurant area (only 2 food businesses within 500 ft). Attend a pre-application meeting with Planning staff to confirm the filing is complete and whether neighborhood notification under §311 is required. Budget 5–8 months from filing to Commission hearing and decision.

outcomes.original: Filing step: If Planning confirms the use is allowed as a continuation or corner-commercial use without a CUA, register the business with the SF Treasurer & Tax Collector to obtain a Business Account Number (BAN). What to say: File online or in person with the entity name, EIN, physical address, and business activity (restaurant). Pay the tiered registration fee based on projected SF gross receipts (e.g., $55 up to $100k for 2023). The BAN is required on every other city permit application, so complete this within 30 days of starting business and before filing the health plan check or building permit.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File a building permit application with the Department of Building Inspection for tenant improvements and change of use, with architectural plans stamped by a California-licensed architect and showing the approved DPH kitchen layout. What to say: Describe the scope: limited cooking equipment, new partitions, electrical and plumbing for sinks and appliances, ADA-compliant restroom upgrades if needed, and change of use from retail to restaurant. Include the DPH-approved plan check and request routing to Planning for zoning referral under §175. If Planning required a CUA, attach the Commission's Motion and say the use is authorized by that decision. Licensed electricians, plumbers and mechanical contractors will pull separate permits for their trades. Budget 2–4 months for plan review and corrections before permit issuance.

outcomes.original: Filing step: During construction, arrange with SFPUC Wastewater Enterprise for grease interceptor sizing and installation review, and file the Installation Verification Form before scheduling the final DBI inspection. What to say: Contact the FOG program after the building permit is issued; SFPUC will assign a Discharger Category (1, 2 or 3) based on the kitchen size and menu, which dictates whether a passive grease trap or hydromechanical interceptor is required. Have the plumber install the device per SFPUC specs and photograph the installation. File the Installation Verification Form to qualify for the 14.2% sewer-bill discount, and keep quarterly maintenance logs on site for inspections.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Two weeks before the planned opening date, schedule the final DPH pre-opening inspection online through the Environmental Health portal, and ensure at least one person has completed the Certified Food Protection Manager exam. What to say: Confirm with your plan reviewer that the facility is at 100% completion: equipment installed and operational, all sinks plumbed with hot and cold water, walls and floors sealed, food stored six inches off the floor, and a certified manager certificate in hand. Walk the space against the DPH checklist before the inspector arrives. If the inspection passes, DPH will issue the permit to operate the same day or within 48 hours; if it fails, corrections must be completed and a reinspection scheduled at $276/hour, delaying opening by 1–3 weeks.
outcomes.note: Record says apply at least one month before (not two weeks), delays are 2-3 weeks (not 1-3), and does not list the specific checklist items or same-day/48-hour issuance timeframe.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File a sign permit application with SF Planning and DBI for any new exterior business signage, awning or illuminated sign, before fabrication or installation. What to say: Submit a photo simulation or elevation drawing showing the sign's size, placement, illumination and materials. Planning reviews for compliance with Article 6 sign controls; in RM-3 districts signs are limited by frontage width and height, and internally illuminated signs may require additional review. Budget 2–6 weeks for approval of a simple storefront sign. Install only after the permit is issued to avoid a notice of violation and removal order.
outcomes.note: Record confirms sign permit with Planning and DBI but does not state the submission requirements, Article 6, RM-3 specifics, timing requirements, or consequences of unpermitted installation.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 0 to 0 days. Estimated government cost: $0 to $0. Notes: No time or government cost is given because the zoning determination is insufficient information: the rules could not decide whether the restaurant use is allowed at 1152 Taylor St in RM-3 zoning without knowing if the property qualifies under Limited Corner Commercial Use (§231) or Limited Commercial Use (§186), and whether the expansion requires a Conditional Use Authorization. If a CUA is required, the timeline from pre-application meeting to Commission decision is typically 5–8 months (120–240 days) based on the 2015 precedent at 1030 Washington St which filed in May and was approved in November 2015 (189 days); CUA fees as of June 2023 started at approximately $2,700 for a no-construction case and scale with project cost. If the use is allowed as a continuation or corner-commercial use, the health permit, building permit and sign permit together take 2–5 months in parallel (building permit 14–120 days, health plan check and permit 35–105 days combined, sign permit 7–45 days) with government fees of approximately $2,100–$18,900 depending on construction valuation: health plan check $828–$2,207, health permit to operate $470, building permit $800–$15,000, and sign permit $300–$1,500. These ranges are for the city approvals only and assume the zoning question is resolved in the operator's favor; if the use is not permitted the concept as described cannot proceed at this address. State business and tax registrations (EIN, entity formation, seller's permit, business registration) add $125–$850 in fees and 1–4 weeks, completed in parallel at project start. Music licensing (ASCAP, BMI) adds $600–$5,000 annually but is not a government permit and takes 1–2 weeks to set up before opening.
